title: Where bond distance is a metric: what is proved
claim: T1: where the bonds of a base satisfy circuit elimination (every parity base), bond distance and bond distance minus one satisfy the triangle inequality (matroid connectivity inside the union of two circuits; b - 1 a pseudometric). T2-T5: bond distance fails it on copies of each of the eight other three-place languages passing K1-K3 (not-all-equal, betweenness, the clause and its twist, R6 and its twist on two knots on four distinctions; R5 and its twist on eight distinctions and six knots). Theorem: among the 34 three-place laws passing K1-K3 (nine languages), bond distance is a metric on every base of copies of one law exactly for parity.
standard_statement: Matroid circuit connectivity (Whitney; Oxley Prop. 4.1.2); minimal non-shattered sets; Horn closure systems (R5).
prior_work: BOND-CHAIN-20261108-001 (chains add nothing on parity laws, A39); KNOT-CIRCUITS-20261020-001 (composes like cycles exactly when affine); FREE-READ-20261118-001 (trees; its referee's parity proof).
